h3. Description of problem

The {{CRDDiscovered}} event reason is defined in {{pkg/util/events.go}} and has a corresponding {{EventRecorder.CRDDiscovered()}} method with a unit test, but it is *never called from any production code path*. This means that when a previously missing CRD is installed and the operator restarts and discovers it, no {{CRDDiscovered}} event is emitted.

In contrast, the {{CRDMissing}} event IS correctly emitted during reconciliation in {{pkg/controller/platform_controller.go:281}} when {{checkCRDGates()}} detects a missing CRD. The asymmetry makes CRD lifecycle observability incomplete: operators and dashboards can see when a CRD goes missing but not when it becomes available.

h3. How reproducible

Always — the event is dead code with zero call sites.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Start autopilot with all CRDs installed
# Remove a managed CRD (e.g., {{machineconfigs.machineconfiguration.openshift.io}})
# Observe {{CRDMissing}} event is emitted (correct)
# Re-install the CRD
# Wait for operator restart and reconciliation
# Check events: no {{CRDDiscovered}} event is emitted

h3. Actual results

No {{CRDDiscovered}} event is ever emitted. The event reason constant and recorder method exist but are unreachable dead code:

* {{pkg/util/events.go:43}} — {{EventReasonCRDDiscovered = "CRDDiscovered"}} (defined)
* {{pkg/util/events.go:164}} — {{func (e *EventRecorder) CRDDiscovered(...)}} (defined)
* Zero call sites in {{pkg/controller/}} or {{pkg/engine/}} or {{cmd/}}

h3. Expected results

When a CRD that was previously missing is discovered during reconciliation (i.e., {{CRDChecker.IsCRDInstalled()}} returns {{true}} for a CRD that was previously {{false}}), a {{CRDDiscovered}} event should be emitted on the HCO object.

h3. Suggested fix

The CRD watcher already detects CRD creation and triggers an operator restart. The {{CRDDiscovered}} event should be emitted either:

# *In the CRD watcher* when it detects a new CRD that is in the managed set, or
# *In* {{checkCRDGates()}} when a CRD gate check passes for a CRD that was previously tracked as missing (requires state tracking in the CRD checker cache)

Option 2 is more consistent with how {{CRDMissing}} is emitted (during reconciliation) and can leverage the existing {{crdCache}} to detect the missing→present transition.

h3. Additional info

The {{missing_dependency}} metric IS correctly updated in both directions (1→0 and 0→1) by {{crd_checker.go:updateDependencyMetric()}}, so the metric side works. Only the event emission is missing for the "discovered" transition.

h2. Summary

The MTV asset template {{assets/active/operators/mtv.yaml.tpl}} cannot be applied against the upstream ForkliftController CRD due to two issues:

# *Wrong field name*: The template uses {{feature_ui}} but the upstream CRD ({{kubev2v/forklift}}) defines the field as {{feature_ui_plugin}}. The CRD has strict decoding enabled, so {{feature_ui}} is rejected as an unknown field.
# *Wrong field types*: The template uses YAML booleans ({{true}}) but the CRD schema defines {{feature_validation}}, {{feature_volume_populator}}, and related fields as {{type: string}} with {{enum: ["true", "false"]}}.

h2. Template content ({{assets/active/operators/mtv.yaml.tpl}})

{code:yaml}apiVersion: forklift.konveyor.io/v1beta1
kind: ForkliftController
metadata:
  name: forklift-controller
  namespace: openshift-mtv
spec:
  feature_ui: true            # CRD field is "feature_ui_plugin", type string
  feature_validation: true     # CRD expects string "true", not boolean
  feature_volume_populator: true  # CRD expects string "true", not boolean{code}

h2. Upstream CRD schema (from {{kubev2v/forklift}})

{code:yaml}feature_ui_plugin:
  default: "true"
  enum: ["true", "false"]
  type: string
feature_validation:
  default: "true"
  enum: ["true", "false"]
  type: string
feature_volume_populator:
  default: "true"
  enum: ["true", "false"]
  type: string{code}

The test CRD at {{test/crds/operators/forklift.konveyor.io_forkliftcontrollers.yaml}} is fetched from upstream via {{hack/update-crds.sh}}, so the CRD is correct.

h2. Reproduction

{code:bash}# With the upstream CRD installed (fetched via hack/update-crds.sh):
kubectl apply -f assets/active/operators/mtv.yaml.tpl
# Error: strict decoding error: unknown field "spec.feature_ui"

# SSA also fails:
# expected string, got &value.valueUnstructured{Value:true}{code}

h2. Impact

* This asset is opt-in (requires {{platform.kubevirt.io/enable-mtv: "true"}} annotation on HCO), so it may never have been applied in CI or production.
* When the opt-in condition is met, the operator logs a {{Reconciler error}} on every reconciliation cycle and the ForkliftController resource is never created.

h2. Found during

E2E test development for asset catalog coverage (branch {{e2e-tombstone}}).

h2. Suggested fix

Update {{assets/active/operators/mtv.yaml.tpl}}:

{code:yaml}spec:
  feature_ui_plugin: "true"
  feature_validation: "true"
  feature_volume_populator: "true"{code}

items.toString: Gating wrapper: DEPLOY_CLUSTER=false ignored when isCloudRun=true (cloud gating)

h2. Summary

When a tier1 gating wrapper job is configured as a cloud gating run ({{isCloudRun=true}}, RHOS cloud in gating-plan), setting {{DEPLOY_CLUSTER=false}} still triggers full deploy/redeploy. User expects {{DEPLOY_CLUSTER=false}} to skip deploy and reuse the given cluster.

h2. Context

* Found during !8955 dev testing
* Jenkins build: dev-verify-cnv-4.20.z-build-tier1-lbednar #17
* Related MR: !8947 introduced {{isCloudRun}} behavior where cloud path always deploys

h2. Root cause (suspected)

Gating wrapper unified Jenkinsfile {{Deploy Clusters}} stage uses:

{code:groovy}
when {
    expression { isCloudRun || env.DEPLOY_CLUSTER.toBoolean() }
}
{code}

Because {{isCloudRun}} is OR'd with {{DEPLOY_CLUSTER}}, cloud runs always enter the deploy stage regardless of the parameter value.

* File: {{contra/cnv/src/jobs/tests/event-triggered/gating/wrapper/Jenkinsfile}} (lines ~206-208)
* Related: {{GatingPipelineConfig.isCloudCluster()}} sets {{isCloudRun=true}} for RHOS cloud clusters in gating-plan

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Configure tier1 gating job with RHOS cloud cluster in gating-plan (cloud gating run, {{isCloudRun=true}})
# Trigger job with {{DEPLOY_CLUSTER=false}} and an existing cluster FQDN in {{CLUSTERS}}
# Observe pipeline execution

h2. Expected result

{{Deploy Clusters}} stage is skipped; job reuses the provided cluster for testing.

h2. Actual result

{{Deploy Clusters}} stage runs and triggers full deploy/redeploy via cloud deploy job ({{ctx.getFactoryConfig().deployJob}}).

h2. Suggested fix (backlog — do not implement yet)

Revisit {{when}} logic so {{DEPLOY_CLUSTER=false}} can skip deploy on cloud runs when a cluster is explicitly provided/reusable. Coordinate with !8947 {{isCloudRun}} semantics and docs in {{skills-catalog/ocp-deployment/references/job-composition.md}}.

h2. References

* [Gating wrapper Jenkinsfile|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/contra/cnv/-/blob/master/src/jobs/tests/event-triggered/gating/wrapper/Jenkinsfile]
* [MR !8947|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/contra/cnv/-/merge_requests/8947]
* [MR !8955|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/contra/cnv/-/merge_requests/8955]

Description of problem:

{noformat} When a VirtualMachineExport resource is created, the status.links.external.cert field is populated with the kube-apiserver CA bundle from the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap instead of the CA that actually signed the exportproxy Route's certificate. This causes any consumer (e.g., MTV/Forklift) that uses this cert to verify the TLS connection to the exportproxy Route to fail with x509: certificate signed by unknown authority{noformat}

Version-Release number of selected component (if applicable):

{noformat} {noformat}

How reproducible:

{noformat} {noformat}

Steps to Reproduce:

{noformat}1.Deploy OpenShift Virtualization on a managed OpenShift cluster (e.g., ROKS on IBM Cloud) where the kube-apiserver CA and the ingress/router CA are distinct (kube-apiserver uses an internal self-signed CA; the router uses a publicly-trusted CA such as Let's Encrypt).

2. Create a VirtualMachineExport for any running VM.

3. Inspect status.links.external.cert:
~~~
oc get vmexport <name> -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.status.links.external.cert}'
~~~

4. Compare with kube-root-ca.crt:

~~~
oc get cm kube-root-ca.crt -n openshift-cnv -o jsonpath='{.data.ca\.crt}'
~~~

5. The two are byte-for-byte identical.

6. Attempt to use the provided cert to connect to the exportproxy Route:

~~~
curl --cacert /tmp/vmexport-cert.pem https://<exportproxy-route-host>/
~~~

7. Connection fails with x509: certificate signed by unknown authority.{noformat}

Actual results:

{noformat} status.links.external.cert is populated with the kube-apiserver CA from kube-root-ca.crt, which has no relationship to the Route's certificate chain. TLS verification fails for any consumer using this field.{noformat}

Expected results:

{noformat} status.links.external.cert should contain the CA that signed the exportproxy Route's TLS certificate, or be left empty when the Route uses a publicly-trusted CA, allowing consumers to fall back to the system trust store.{noformat}

Additional info:

{noformat} Upstream References
KubeVirt source: https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/pkg/storage/export/export/links.go — routeCAConfigMapName = "kube-root-ca.crt", getRouteCert(), findCertByHostName(){noformat}

items.fromString:
h2. What needs to be done

_1. Run-name_: update {{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}}'s {{run-name}} to include {{github.ref_name}} alongside {{cluster_name}}, mirroring the {{[cluster_name] @ branch}} convention already used in {{deploy-manual-console.yml}}.

_2. Add {{workflow_call}} to {{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}}_, alongside its existing {{workflow_dispatch}}, with matching inputs and an explicit {{secrets:}} list ({{IC_KEY}} required; {{OPENSHIFT_PULL_SECRET}}, {{ARC_GITHUB_APP_ID}}, {{ARC_GITHUB_APP_INSTALL_ID}}, {{ARC_GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY}}, {{ARC_GITHUB_PAT}}, {{CLUSTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD}}, {{SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}} optional) -- mirrors the dual-trigger pattern already used in {{ibmc-cluster-teardown.yml}}.

_3. Add a {{precheck}} job to {{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}}_ that re-probes DNS for cluster existence right after the concurrency lock is acquired, and skips {{provision-cluster}} if another caller already finished building it. Closes a double-provisioning race that splitting {{hot-cluster-check.yml}} into separate jobs would otherwise introduce, and also protects against today's zero-protection double {{workflow_dispatch}} case.

_4. Split {{hot-cluster-check.yml}}'s single {{check-and-provision}} job into three_: {{probe}} (existing DNS check, no concurrency) -> {{provision}} (holds the {{hot-cluster-provision-<cluster_name>}} concurrency lock, calls {{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}} natively via {{uses:}} + {{secrets: inherit}}) -> {{result}} (computes final {{cluster_ready}} output, writes step summary).

_5. Verify callers unaffected_: only {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}'s {{cluster-check}} job calls {{hot-cluster-check.yml}}, and it only depends on job result (success/failure), not the {{cluster_ready}} output value -- safe to restructure.

h2. Why

{{hot-cluster-check.yml}} currently provisions the hot cluster via {{createWorkflowDispatch}} (a REST API call that starts a completely separate, disconnected workflow run), then polls it and only posts a plain-text link in a job summary. GitHub only visually nests a sub-workflow into a run's job tree when it's invoked as a reusable workflow ({{uses:}}), so today the actual multi-hour cluster build is invisible in the Checks tab of both the PR that triggers it and any PRs that queue behind it (they just show a generic "Queued" status with no context). Converting to a native {{uses:}} call makes the build show up as a real, expandable, descriptively-named job everywhere it's relevant.

items.fromString:
h2. What needs to be done

Add a single, always-visible PR check (via the GitHub Checks API, not just a job name) whose {{output.title}}/{{summary}} text is explicitly rewritten as the hot-cluster E2E pipeline progresses through phases, e.g.:

* "Waiting for cluster to be built"
* "Running gating tests"
* "Passed" / "Failed"

This needs a small, long-running reporter step/job with {{checks:write}} permission that calls {{checks.update}} at each phase transition -- new infrastructure, distinct from a regular job's static name/status.

h2. Context

Follow-up to the fix that makes hot-cluster provisioning show up as a nested job (via a native {{uses:}} reusable-workflow call in {{hot-cluster-check.yml}}, instead of a REST-API dispatch-and-poll that's invisible in the PR's Checks tab). That fix makes the underlying work visible if you expand the job tree, but doesn't give a single glanceable check narrating the current phase the way this ticket describes.

Existing required checks (e.g. {{verify-gating-tests}} / "Run Gating Tests" in {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}) only compute their name once, statically, before the run starts -- they don't dynamically rewrite their own description as phases progress, so there's no existing precedent for this pattern in the repo yet.
items.toString:
h2. What needs to be done

This ticket covers *all* known issues with how the hot-cluster E2E pipeline ({{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}) presents itself in a PR's Checks tab. There are two distinct problems, both rooted in the same underlying gap: none of our checks communicate _which phase_ the pipeline is in or _why_ they look the way they do.

h3. Problem 1: No single glanceable check narrating pipeline phase

Add a single, always-visible PR check (via the GitHub Checks API, not just a job name) whose {{output.title}}/{{summary}} text is explicitly rewritten as the hot-cluster E2E pipeline progresses through phases, e.g.:

* "Waiting for cluster to be built"
* "Running gating tests"
* "Passed" / "Failed"

This needs a small, long-running reporter step/job with {{checks:write}} permission that calls {{checks.update}} at each phase transition -- new infrastructure, distinct from a regular job's static name/status.

Follow-up context: this is a follow-up to the fix that makes hot-cluster provisioning show up as a nested job (via a native {{uses:}} reusable-workflow call in {{hot-cluster-check.yml}}, instead of a REST-API dispatch-and-poll that's invisible in the PR's Checks tab). That fix makes the underlying work visible if you expand the job tree, but doesn't give a single glanceable check narrating the current phase the way this section describes.

h3. Problem 2: Existing checks show broken or fragmented names on "irrelevant" events

Investigation (July 2026) found that on PRs, the Checks tab for {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}} can show confusing entries, especially on no-op trigger events (e.g. a {{labeled}} event for a label other than {{ok-to-test}}):

*2a. `verify-gating-tests` renders as a raw, unevaluated expression instead of readable text.*

{code:yaml}  verify-gating-tests:
    name: ${{ (github.event.action != 'labeled' || github.event.label.name == 'ok-to-test') && 'Run Gating Tests' || 'Run Gating Tests (skipped - irrelevant label event)' }}
    needs: [check-trust, cluster-check, cluster-health-check, run-e2e-tests]
    if: |
      always() &&
      (github.event.action != 'labeled' || github.event.label.name == 'ok-to-test'){code}

Root cause: this job's own {{if:}} skips it entirely for irrelevant label events. GitHub Actions only evaluates dynamic {{name:}} expressions on the *runner*, as the job starts executing. When a job is skipped (never dispatched to a runner because its {{if:}} was false), there's no runner to do that evaluation, so the orchestration service falls back to displaying the *raw, unevaluated ternary string* as the check name instead of either branch's text. This is a confirmed, long-standing GitHub Actions limitation (see [actions/runner#1215|https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/1215], closed as won't-fix: "skipped jobs events are never sent to the runner"). The irony is that the dynamic name was specifically designed to show a friendly "(skipped - irrelevant label event)" message for exactly this case, but because the job is skipped, that text can never actually render.

_Fix direction:_ don't rely on a job-level {{if:}} to represent the "irrelevant event" case for any job whose identity depends on a dynamic {{name:}}. Instead, let {{verify-gating-tests}} always run (drop the label check from the job's {{if:}}, keep only {{always()}} plus the trust/cluster-outcome logic it already needs), and move the "is this an irrelevant label event" short-circuit into the job's first step ({{exit 0}} immediately with a clear log line). Because the job then always reaches a runner, its dynamic {{name:}} expression always evaluates correctly.

*2b. `cluster-check` fragments into unrelated check contexts depending on whether it ran.*

{{cluster-check}} is a {{uses:}}-based job (calls {{hot-cluster-check.yml}} as a reusable workflow) gated by its own {{if:}}. When skipped, GitHub reports a single bare context named {{cluster-check}}. When it actually runs, GitHub instead reports one context *per job inside the called workflow* (e.g. {{cluster-check / probe}}, {{cluster-check / provision}}, {{cluster-check / result}}) -- there is no single {{cluster-check}} context in the executed case at all. These are fundamentally different check contexts by GitHub design (a {{uses:}} job's sub-jobs each get their own compound-named check when they run), so this fragmentation *cannot be fixed by renaming alone* -- there's no name that GitHub will report identically in both the skipped and executed cases.

_Fix direction (needs design):_ avoid ever showing the bare skipped {{cluster-check}} context by not gating the outer {{uses:}} call with a job-level {{if:}} tied to "is this event relevant" at all. Instead, always call {{hot-cluster-check.yml}} unconditionally, and push the "should we even probe/provision" decision into an input consumed by {{hot-cluster-check.yml}}'s own first job ({{probe}}), which already always runs today. {{probe}} would short-circuit quickly (and cheaply) when told the event is irrelevant, so PRs would consistently see the same compound-named contexts ({{cluster-check / probe}}, ...) succeed quickly instead of alternating between a bare skipped context and a compound executed one. This requires adding a {{should_run}} (or similar) input to {{hot-cluster-check.yml}} and threading it through from {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}; scope this properly before implementing, since it touches the reusable workflow's public interface (also used by other callers).

h3. Acceptance criteria

* A single always-present PR check clearly narrates the current phase of the hot-cluster E2E pipeline (waiting for cluster / running gating tests / passed / failed), updated live via the Checks API.
* {{verify-gating-tests}} never renders as a raw unevaluated expression string in the Checks tab -- it always shows readable text, including for irrelevant-label no-op events.
* {{cluster-check}} (and any other {{uses:}}-based job in this pipeline) does not alternate between a bare skipped context and a compound executed context across different trigger events for the same logical check; irrelevant-event runs are fast, clearly labeled, and consistently named.
* No regression to {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}'s existing required-check semantics (branch protection continues to key off the correct, stable context names).

h3. Context

Existing required checks (e.g. {{verify-gating-tests}} / "Run Gating Tests" in {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}) only compute their name once, statically or dynamically, before/as the run starts -- they don't dynamically rewrite their own description as phases progress, and (per Problem 2) the dynamic-name mechanism itself is unreliable when the job can be skipped. There's no existing precedent in the repo for a check that safely narrates progress across its own lifetime; this ticket establishes that pattern.

items.fromString:
h2. What needs to be done

Four separate implementations of "delete IBM Cloud VPC-infrastructure resources for a cluster" exist and have drifted (each with bugs the others don't have), leaving orphaned VPCs/subnets/security groups/load balancers/custom images/COS instances behind across multiple hot-cluster generations:

* {{ci-scripts/hot-cluster/cleanup-ipi-resources.sh}} — proactive cleanup before every IPI setup run
* {{ci-scripts/hot-cluster/create-ipi-cluster.sh}} — partial (COS+images only) inline cleanup between retry attempts
* {{.github/workflows/ibmc-cluster-teardown.yml}} — "Clean up VPC resources" step, uses an exact-match VPC lookup that never matches a real VPC name (dead code)
* {{.github/workflows/ibmc-cleanup-all.yml}} — its own inline duplicate

* Extract one shared, configurable script ({{cleanup-vpc-resources.sh}}) as the single source of truth for VPC-resource cleanup by cluster-name prefix, with {{DRY_RUN}} and {{CLEAN_VPC}} toggles.
* Fix the exact-match VPC lookup bug, missing {{kube-*}}-prefixed load balancer handling, and missing custom-image/COS-instance cleanup.
* Update all four call sites to delegate to the shared script instead of reimplementing.
* Add guaranteed backstop sweeps (after {{openshift-install destroy cluster}} and on setup failure) so a missing/expired install-state artifact no longer means zero cleanup happens.

h2. Why

Orphaned IBM Cloud resources (VPCs, subnets, security groups, load balancers, custom RHCOS images, Cloud Object Storage instances) accumulated silently across multiple failed hot-cluster setup attempts, since no single cleanup path was a complete safety net on its own.

items.toString: Hot cluster E2E reruns unnecessarily on unrelated label events

items.fromString:
h2. Problem 1: any label addition retriggers the full E2E chain

{{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}} triggers on {{pull_request_target: types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled]}}. GitHub Actions cannot filter the {{labeled}} type by _which_ label was added, so *any* label addition -- bot-added {{lgtm}}, {{approved}}, {{jira/valid-reference}}, etc., not just {{ok-to-test}} -- starts a full new run.

For a trusted (OWNERS-listed) or same-repo author, {{cluster-check}}'s {{if:}} grants a pass regardless of which event triggered it, so every unrelated label re-provisions the cluster, rebuilds the plugin image, and reruns the full Playwright suite. Confirmed live: adding {{lgtm}} to PR #4261 spawned a brand new run that rebuilt the image and reran tests from scratch, purely from the label.

Worse, combined with the {{Run Gating Tests}} required-check rollup added in CNV-92582 (which uses {{if: always()}} so it never silently vanishes), this created a regression risk: if a trusted PR's E2E had already passed, a later unrelated label (e.g. {{lgtm}}) would spawn a new run whose {{cluster-check}} skips (nothing changed) -- but the rollup's unconditional {{always()}} would still run, see {{run-e2e-tests}} skipped, and report *failure*, overwriting the prior passing result for that same commit SHA with a bogus one.

There's also a related pre-existing bug this interacts with: {{concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true}} was unconditional, so an irrelevant label event immediately cancelled any real in-progress run (this is the same root cause CNV-92566 previously worked around by removing an event-relevance guard -- which is why simply reinstating that guard alone would not have been safe).

h3. Fix

In {{.github/workflows/hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}:

* Made {{concurrency.cancel-in-progress}} conditional: {{${{ github.event.action != 'labeled' || github.event.label.name == 'ok-to-test' }}}} -- irrelevant labels queue behind a real run instead of cancelling it.
* Reinstated the event-relevance guard on {{cluster-check}}'s {{if:}} (safe now that cancellation no longer clobbers real runs).
* Applied the same guard to the {{verify-gating-tests}} ({{Run Gating Tests}}) rollup's {{if:}}, so it does not run -- and therefore cannot post a competing result -- for irrelevant label events, leaving the last meaningful run's result as authoritative.

Validated via a truth-table simulation across {{opened}}/{{synchronize}}/{{reopened}} (trusted and untrusted), {{workflow_dispatch}}, {{labeled}}+{{ok-to-test}} (the untrusted-fork unlock case), and {{labeled}}+{{lgtm}}/{{approved}}/{{jira/valid-reference}} (trusted and untrusted) -- all resolve as intended, including the specific regression scenario.

h2. Problem 2: pending E2E keeps running after a PR is closed/force-merged

Nothing cancels an in-progress {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}} run when its PR is merged or closed -- the workflow only listens to {{opened}}/{{synchronize}}/{{reopened}}/{{labeled}}, not {{closed}}, so a force-merge (admin bypass) leaves the cluster provisioning / image build / Playwright run going to completion for a PR that no longer exists, wasting cluster and CI time.

h3. Fix

Added a new, dedicated workflow {{.github/workflows/hot-cluster-e2e-cancel-on-close.yml}} ({{pull_request_target: types: [closed]}}, fires on merge or plain close) that looks up any in-progress/queued {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}} runs for that PR (matching by {{pull_requests}} array, {{head_sha}}, or {{head_branch}} -- same lookup pattern as {{retest-e2e.yml}}) and cancels them via the Actions API. Cancelling the top-level run cascades to cancel all nested reusable-workflow jobs ({{cluster-check}}, {{run-e2e-tests}}, {{verify-gating-tests}}).

Kept as a separate file rather than extending {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}} itself, to avoid the {{closed}} action flowing through that file's already-intricate trust-gate / event-relevance conditions.

*Explicitly out of scope*: cancelling the separately-dispatched {{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}} provisioning run that {{hot-cluster-check.yml}} may have kicked off when no cluster existed yet -- that run is only identifiable by {{cluster_name}}, which could be shared by other concurrent PRs, so auto-cancelling it safely needs separate design.

Not yet committed/pushed as of ticket creation.

This work item links to "kubevirt-ui/kubevirt-plugin#4260: CNV-92582: Hot Cluster E2E required check does not actually block merges to main (Web Link)"

items.fromString:
h2. Problem

{{main}}'s branch protection lists {{Run Gating Tests}} as a required status check, but it has never actually blocked a merge -- confirmed against real, already-merged PRs, including cases where the hot cluster E2E job genuinely ran and failed.

h3. Direct evidence

* *PR #4221* ({{CNV-92152-organize-hot-cluster-scripts}}, author {{galkremer1}}, an OWNERS approver, same-repo): the {{Run Gating Tests}} job actually executed and *genuinely failed* a real Playwright test run. The PR merged to {{main}} 140 minutes later anyway.
* *PR #4218* / *PR #4219* (same author): an upstream image-build step failed, cascading to {{Run Gating Tests}} being skipped. Both merged within minutes.
* *PR #4240* ({{bmaio-redhat}}, an OWNERS-listed reviewer, opened from a personal fork): the entire E2E chain ({{cluster-check}} → {{Cluster Health Check}} → {{Run E2E Tests}}) was skipped because the (now-fixed) trust-gate logic misclassified him as untrusted. Merged with E2E never having run.

h3. Root cause

Two independent, compounding issues:

# *Naming mismatch (primary cause):* the job that runs Playwright is named {{Run Gating Tests}} but lives _inside_ the reusable workflow {{hot-cluster-e2e-run.yml}}, invoked via {{uses:}} from the {{run-e2e-tests}} job in {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}. GitHub always posts nested reusable-workflow jobs under a composite name, so the real check-run context is {{Run E2E Tests / Run Gating Tests}} -- which has *never matched* the bare {{Run Gating Tests}} string branch protection requires. This mismatch dates back to the original hot-cluster CI POC ({{efe130dc5}}), before the job moved into a reusable workflow; branch protection was never updated to match.
# *Silent-skip cascades:* upstream {{if:}} conditions on {{cluster-check}} / {{cluster-health-check}} / {{run-e2e-tests}} (trust-gate, {{ok-to-test}} label, cluster health) cause the whole chain to report {{skipped}} rather than an explicit failure when preconditions aren't met, so even if the naming matched, a skip wouldn't reliably block merge.

h3. Fix (implemented in the {{CNV-91457-support-concurrent-hot-clusters}} branch, pending push)

* Renamed the nested Playwright job in {{hot-cluster-e2e-run.yml}} from {{Run Gating Tests}} to {{Playwright Gating Tests}} (context becomes {{Run E2E Tests / Playwright Gating Tests}}).
* Added a new *top-level* job {{verify-gating-tests}} ({{name: Run Gating Tests}}) directly in {{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}, with {{if: always()}} and {{needs: [check-trust, cluster-check, cluster-health-check, run-e2e-tests]}}. Being top-level (not invoked via {{uses:}}), it posts its check-run under the bare {{Run Gating Tests}} name -- exactly matching what branch protection already requires, so no branch-protection/GitHub Settings change is needed.
* The job passes only when {{needs.run-e2e-tests.result == 'success'}}; any other outcome (skip, failure, cancellation) is now an explicit, always-reported failure that blocks merge -- regardless of trust.
* Existing OWNERS-based trust-gate and {{ok-to-test}} label mechanics are unchanged: non-OWNERS authors still only get E2E to run once a maintainer applies {{ok-to-test}} (removed again on each push by {{ok-to-test-reset.yml}}); the difference is that failing to do so now blocks merge instead of silently passing.
* Validated via YAML/bash syntax checks and by simulating {{needs.*.result}} combinations against the real historical PRs above (confirms PR #4221/#4240-style cases would now correctly block).

No changes needed to {{openshift/release}} Tide/Prow config -- confirmed the required-context list is a plain GitHub branch-protection setting for this repo, not Prow/Tide-managed.

items.fromString:
*Environment*

CNV: v4.22.3.rhel9-18
OCP: 4.22.4

*Description*

When performing a storage live migration on a running Windows 11 VM with vTPM enabled, the VM boot time changes - sometimes.

{noformat}```
AssertionError: Boot time changed for VMs:
{'windows-11-vm-1783578359-359099': {
'initial': 'Workstation Statistics for \\DESKTOP-B7L8R67\r\nStatistics since 7/9/2026 6:32:13 AM\r\n', 
'current': 'Workstation Statistics for \\DESKTOP-B7L8R67\r\nStatistics since 7/9/2026 6:33:07 AM\r\n'}}
```{noformat}

No `GuestPanicked` events are recorded, suggesting the reboot may be caused by improper vTPM state handling during live migration.

*How reproducible:*
The failure is not consistent. 
This issue was reproduced overall *3 times* (hostpath-csi to OCS) in CNV versions *4.20* and *4.22*

*Steps to Reproduce*

Automates test - {{test_vm_storage_class_migration_windows_vm_with_vtpm_not_restarted}}

1. Deploy a Windows 11 VM with vTPM enabled on a cluster with multiple storage classes (e.g., hostpath-csi-basic and ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization).
2. Start the VM and wait for it to fully boot.
3. Record the VM's boot time via `net statistics workstation`.
4. Initiate a storage class migration from the source storage class to the target storage class.
5. Wait for the storage migration to complete.
6. Check the VM's boot time again via `net statistics workstation`.



*Expected Behavior*

The VM's boot time should remain unchanged, indicating no reboot occurred during the migration process.

*Actual Behavior*

The VM reboots during the live migration phase of the storage class migration. The boot time changes from `6:32:13 AM` to `6:33:07 AM` (a 54-second gap corresponding to the new virt-launcher pod starting). The error message:

```
AssertionError: Boot time changed for VMs:
{'windows-11-vm-1783578359-359099': {'initial': 'Workstation Statistics for \\DESKTOP-B7L8R67\r\nStatistics since 7/9/2026 6:32:13 AM\r\n', 'current': 'Workstation Statistics for \\DESKTOP-B7L8R67\r\nStatistics since 7/9/2026 6:33:07 AM\r\n'}}
```

*Evidence*

**Timeline of events:**

* 06:32:33Z: Boot time captured (Statistics since 7/9/2026 6:32:13 AM)
* 06:32:34Z: Storage migration plan created
* 06:32:53Z: workload-update-controller triggers kubevirt-workload-update migration
* 06:33:07Z: New virt-launcher pod starts on target node cnvqe-043
* 06:33:10Z: libvirt starts up in new virt-launcher pod (version 11.10.0)
* 06:34:28Z: Live migration completes (SuccessfulMigration event)
* 06:35:03Z: Storage migration plan marked Completed
* 06:35:11Z: Test detects boot time change (Statistics since 7/9/2026 6:33:07 AM)

**Cluster events:**
```

reason: SuccessfulCreate
reportingComponent: workload-update-controller
```

```
message: The VirtualMachineInstance migrated to node cnvqe-043.***MASKED***.
reason: Migrated
```

```
reason: SuccessfulMigration
firstTimestamp: "2026-07-09T06:34:28Z"
```

**Storage migration status:**
```
status:
completedMigrations:

* windows-11-vm-1783578359-359099
  phase: Completed
```

**Libvirt restart confirmation:**
```
2026-07-09 06:33:10.273+0000: starting up libvirt version: 11.10.0
```

**No guest panic events recorded:**
```
items: []
```



*Affected Component*

**Component:** kubevirt workload-update-controller / migration controller
**Suspected code path:** vTPM state handling during live migration triggered by storage class migration workflow. The absence of GuestPanicked events combined with the clean reboot pattern suggests the vTPM device state is not being properly preserved or migrated, causing the Windows guest to perform a clean reboot rather than crash.

Jenkins build: [https://jenkins-csb-cnvqe-main.dno.corp.redhat.com/job/test-pytest-t3-cnv-4.22-storage-hppcsiblock/47/|https://jenkins-csb-cnvqe-main.dno.corp.redhat.com/job/test-pytest-t3-cnv-4.22-storage-hppcsiblock/47/]

h2. [Bug 1|https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1]: Trusted authors' E2E incorrectly skipped on non-{{ok-to-test}} labeled events

{{hot-cluster-e2e.yml}}'s {{cluster-check}} job condition ANDed a standalone labeled-event gate on top of the trust-gate:

{noformat}if: |
  always() &&
  (github.event.action != 'labeled' || github.event.label.name == 'ok-to-test') &&
  (
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
    github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository ||
    needs.check-trust.outputs.trusted == 'true' ||
    (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name == 'ok-to-test')
  ){noformat}

Since bots ({{openshift-ci[bot]}}) routinely add labels like {{lgtm}}/{{approved}}/{{jira/valid-reference}} as part of normal PR lifecycle automation, every one of those routine label additions silently skipped the entire E2E workflow — even for fully trusted collaborators. Confirmed on a real run: PR #4253 (author {{mayarub}}, {{author_association=COLLABORATOR}}, confirmed trusted by the {{Check Trusted Author}} job), labeled {{lgtm}} by the bot → {{cluster-check}} and everything downstream still skipped.

*Fix*: removed the redundant standalone clause. The trust-gate's existing 4th branch ({{action == 'labeled' && label == 'ok-to-test'}}) already correctly handles unlocking untrusted/fork PRs; the {{ok-to-test}} gate for untrusted authors is unaffected — only the incorrect extra blocking of trusted/same-repo authors was removed.

h2. [Bug 2|https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2]: Auto-teardown cluster discovery never actually found IPI clusters

{{ibmc-cluster-auto-teardown.yml}}'s {{discover-clusters}} job's "Setup IBM Cloud CLI" step only installed the {{kubernetes-service}} plugin, never {{cis}}. Every {{ibmcloud cis}} call in that job ({{instances}}, {{instance-set}}, {{domains}}, {{dns-records}}) then failed silently (swallowed by {{2>/dev/null || true}}), producing a misleading {{WARNING: No CIS instance found}} instead of surfacing the real "plugin not installed" error — so DNS-based IPI cluster discovery never worked, even with real clusters/DNS records present. Introduced when the {{discover-clusters}} job was added as part of CNV-91457's multi-cluster support; the DNS-lookup logic was modeled on {{cleanup-ipi-resources.sh}}/{{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}} but missed carrying over their {{ibmcloud plugin install cis -f}} step.

*Fix*: added the missing {{Install CIS plugin}} step, matching the existing working pattern in {{ibmc-cleanup-all.yml}}. ROKS discovery (the {{ibmcloud oc cluster ls}} half) was unaffected.

h2. [Bug 3|https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=3]: jq crash when matching both direct and {{kube-}}-prefixed load balancer names (multi-cluster resource cleanup)

Found while running {{ibmc-cleanup-all.yml}} for real against the live hot-cluster infrastructure to verify complete resource deletion (VMs, LBs, subnets, gateways, security groups, DNS, VPC, images, COS). Both {{ibmc-cleanup-all.yml}} ("Wait for LB deletions" step) and {{ci-scripts/hot-cluster/cleanup-ipi-resources.sh}} (used by {{ibmc-cluster-setup.yml}}'s "Clean up stale IPI resources" step) contained the same latent jq logic bug:

{noformat}select(.name | startswith($cn) or (.name | startswith("kube-" + $cn))){noformat}

Piping {{.name}} into context first means the right-hand side of {{or}} re-applies {{.name}} to the _already-extracted string_ (i.e. attempts {{"somestring".name}}), which jq cannot do. Since jq's {{or}} short-circuits, this only triggers when a given load balancer's name does *not* match {{$cn}} directly, forcing evaluation of the buggy right branch — exactly the case whenever another cluster's own load balancers (including its {{kube-}}-prefixed ones) coexist alongside the one being targeted. Confirmed via a real crash: {{jq: error (at <stdin>:708): Cannot index string with string "name"}}, exit code 5, which (under {{set -e}}/{{pipefail}}, active by default for GitHub Actions {{run:}} steps) aborted the whole step and skipped every remaining deletion step (subnets, gateways, floating IPs, security groups, DNS, VPC) without any indication of what was and wasn’t cleaned up.

This is exactly the kind of bug the concurrent multi-cluster work (CNV-91457) surfaces that wouldn’t have shown up with only one cluster ever existing at a time.

*Fix*: parenthesize each {{.name | startswith(...)}} independently so {{.}} is reset to the root object for each check: {{(.name | startswith($cn)) or (.name | startswith("kube-" + $cn))}}. Also hardened every other {{ibmcloud is ... --output json | jq ...}} pipeline in {{ibmc-cleanup-all.yml}} with a {{select(type == "object")}} guard, since a transient/malformed API response could otherwise crash any of them the same way.

Validated by reproducing the exact real-world data shape (mixed matching/non-matching/{{kube-}}-prefixed load balancer names across two coexisting clusters) against the corrected jq expression locally — confirmed correct counts with no errors.

Not yet committed/pushed as of ticket update — pending confirmation before pushing to {{main}}.
